text:
tyler: quick heads-up — saw large steady GPU memory growth when running long-context chat workloads with async eviction throttling enabled on the AMD nodes this morning

maria: hmm that's new. which throttle? the new 'evict_batch_delay_ms' flag?

tyler: yeah, set to 12ms in the autoscaler profile for Dedicated pools. repro with a 50k token continuous stream (simulated user replay). growth hits ~10GB over 1hr and then OOM on some cards

aj: logs? traces?

tyler: pasted simplified logs from benchbot run:

```
2026-03-10T09:12:03Z bench: start replay run id=run-842
2026-03-10T09:12:35Z kvcache: async-evict queued pages=128 pending=3
2026-03-10T09:13:42Z kvmgr: alloc_shard failed size=67108864 err=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-03-10T09:13:42Z runtime: fallback to small-quant kernels
2026-03-10T10:05:01Z bench: mark progress tokens=50000
```

sam: interesting that runtime fell back to small-quant kernels — could be downstream from allocation failures
maria: we should check page table fragmentation and stale owner refs. did you capture page table walk traces?
tyler: yes — attaching short snippet from tracelog (KVPageTable events):

```
PT_LOOKUP shard=7 addr=0x7f45cb0000 state=FREE
PT_ALLOC shard=7 page_id=282 owner=stream-18
PT_MAP shard=7 page_id=282 gpu_ptr=0x7fffa00000
PT_EVICT queued=1 reason=throttle
PT_LOOKUP shard=7 addr=0x7f45cb0000 state=MAPPED
PT_SHADOW_ALLOC shard=7 page_id=282 owner=stream-34
```

aj: PT_SHADOW_ALLOC entries are suspicious. looks like we may be double-allocating during async eviction windows

maria: are these AMD nodes only? Tyler said a mix earlier
tyler: repro ratio is much higher on AMD MI250 nodes; smaller on NV H100 but still present under heavy longctx with many small writes to KV cache

benchbot: perf-summary run-842: p50 latency +8%, p95 +22%, mem-increase-rate 9.3MB/min (AMD), 1.4MB/min (NV)

sam: that 9.3MB/min -> 10GB/hour matches the OOM timing. suspect reuse bookkeeping is missing decrement on evict for async case

maria: also saw PCIe stall counters bumping in AMD nodes during the microburst evict windows (maybe PCIe flushes causing ordering differences)

aj: could be ordering: we move page ownership to shadow owner then schedule GPU free on a different stream; if the GPU free completes after a re-map, pointer reuse can be wrong -> ghost refs

tyler: I ran a capture with nvprof/rocprof and saw repeated kernel selection toggles around the time of the alloc failures — runtime moves between full-kernels and fallback kernels mid-request

maria: kernel selection toggles could be a symptom, not cause. fallback happens after oom; oom happens after double-alloc or missing free. but toggles might amplify perf regressions (different memory layouts)

aj: proposal: add an atomic epoch to page table entries that increments on every eviction cycle. reclaim path must check epoch to avoid reusing entries that are in-flight for GPU frees. also serialize shadow-alloc path behind a light stripe lock per-shard for the async path only

sam: sounds good. also add a diagnostic counter for "shadow_alloc_race" and emit a short stack/log when hit. we need telemetry to triage in prod

tyler: i have a small repro harness that triggers it under --evict_delay 12ms and --write-sparsity 0.02. i'll push to eng-runtime/bench-repro and attach run script

benchbot: uploaded artifact run-842 to s3://redwood-bench/repodata/run-842.tgz (sha256: b3c4...)

maria: quick mitigation path: increase evict_batch_delay to 100ms or disable async eviction on AMD pools until fix lands. can we do a hotfix that makes async evict fallback to sync evict when shadow_alloc count > 0?
aj: yes, we can gate async path with a safe-check: if there are pending frees or PT_SHADOW entries for a given shard then disable async batching for that shard. cheap and low-risk

tyler: can we also add a CI perf test that runs the longctx microburst for 30min on both archs? catches regressions earlier than current 5min tests
maria: agreed. add it to perf-nightly on an opt-in AMD runner for now

sam: assignable tasks?
maria: i'll own the patch for epoch+safe-check and telemetry (PR ready by EOD tomorrow)
aj: i'll own the stripe-lock and unit tests for the sync fallback (start tomorrow AM)
tyler: i'll maintain the repro harness and add the new perf CI job (small infra change)

infra-bot: created tasks: RW-1193 (pt-epoch-evict-check), RW-1194 (async-evict-locks), RW-1195 (longctx-perf-ci)
tyler: one more note — kernel selection heuristics may need a small tweak to avoid toggling mid-request when memory pressure is transient. i'll open a follow-up with logs showing timelines

maria: thanks team. urgent mitigation: ops, please relax evict async on AMD pools for the next 24h
sam: pinging ops in #eng-infra

ops-note: (from ops) we've temporarily disabled async-evict on amd-dedicated pool at 2026-03-10T16:10:00Z

tyler: confirmed reduced growth in the next run (mem-increase-rate dropped to ~0.9MB/min). we'll iterate on the fix

aj: TL;DR: race in async eviction + page table shadowing causes ghost allocations on some GPUs; mitigation gated async path; fix: epoch-check + per-shard async-gate + telemetry + longer perf CI runs

maria: leaving this thread open until PR merged and perf CI green :thumbsup:
